key_insight: Universal alloy potentials can approach cross-database DFT agreement, making benchmark controls essential for interpreting model rankings.
engineering_relevance: For alloy screening, checking elemental references and DFT database disagreement helps distinguish model errors from benchmark artifacts.
method: Benchmark 14 universal ML interatomic potentials on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against AFLOW, unseen during training.
Compare energy and stability errors with disagreement among AFLOW, Alexandria, and OQMD.
Re-reference energies and screen broken elemental references to test ranking robustness.
evidence_signal: Half the structures show DFT disagreement below 6–8 meV/atom, but averages reach 16–30 meV/atom; after re-referencing, the best model matches Alexandria’s agreement with AFLOW.
watch_item: DFT database disagreement limits measurable accuracy, so small ranking differences should not be treated as definitive model superiority.
paper_title: How good are universal MLIPs for alloys? A benchmark is only as trustworthy as its controls
